rationale: The aftermath receipt executed and is read as-is: the forgery is accepted in both streams of the file (indices 13 and 22) and the higher-term leadership outcome is reproduced (index 25), while the three bound comparisons came out unknown because of a defect on my side, not the target's - one of the two streams' campaign-request events omitted the identity field my prerequisite required, so the admission of that event could not be correlated (diagnostic at index 11: 'Missing operation admission fields or identity'). I record the child-level account with the receipt's real witnesses, state plainly that the aftermath bounds are unmeasured here, and request one successor of the same fixed experiment (previous_id e4fc0a862aa0426eb128344d68ef7b76-experiment, same investigation) with only that field added so the bounds are actually evaluated: the corrected harness produces the field on both streams and passes locally.

interpretations.rationale: What this receipt settles about the aftermath question: the acceptance defect and its electoral consequence reproduce independently of the earlier two receipts in the same file, at indices 13 (quorum stream) and 22 (aftermath stream) for the accepted peer-form MsgForgetLeader and index 25 for the candidate becoming StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent is still serving, so the mechanism is not an artefact of one scenario. What it does not settle is the bound I actually wanted from this experiment: whether the deposed incumbent sheds leadership and accepts an anchor at the committed prefix. Those three comparisons are unknown, and the receipt's own diagnostics attribute the gap to my prerequisite specification (event 11 lacks the campaign identity field required by the admission alias, hence 'Missing operation admission fields or identity'), not to missing target behaviour; the raw aftermath observation at index 26 exists (the incumbent becomes StateFollower at term 3 with lead 3 and its append anchored at prev=(10,1) was accepted with response index 11) but is deliberately not counted, because an uncorrelated observation is not evidence for a comparison. Bounds on the harm therefore remain open for this question and are re-requested with the corrected fixed experiment; the disruption half of the defect (a healthy leader replaced at a higher term after one accepted message) is already supported by three receipts.
counterevidence: The three bound comparisons came out unknown, so this receipt must not be read as showing that no committed entry is lost or that the incumbent always concedes; that remains unmeasured.
The gap is harness-side: the diagnostics name my missing identity field on event 11, so the unknown outcomes are not target counterevidence.
limitations: Only the acceptance and the higher-term leadership outcome are cited; the incumbent-demotion and prefix-anchor observations are visible but uncorrelated and are not used.

The harness prefix means the incumbent's committed index is 10 and its term-2 entry at index 11 stays uncommitted, so 'committed prefix intact' can only be asserted at index 10 for this configuration.
Fault-model assumption unchanged: a peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the documented inbound path.

scope.description: Unchanged from the previous revision: three test functions in one file; the third runs the forged election to completion and then delivers the new leader's first append to the deposed incumbent through the public Step path, observing the incumbent's soft state, the append anchor and the acknowledgement.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step.
Only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire.
All nodes start from the same storage snapshot (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}); the incumbent's committed prefix is (index=10, term=1) and its term-2 entry at index 11 stays uncommitted.
The new leader's own commit value is emitted as raw data only; no comparison depends on it.
excluded: Any claim about the new leader's commit index (per-peer Match is not fully observable through the public API here).

experiment.prefix: Run all three TestAssurance functions. The third repeats the election, heartbeat, under-lease control, forged message, re-delivered pre-vote and vote, then takes the new leader's first MsgApp, delivers it to the deposed incumbent and emits the incumbent's post-append soft state with the append anchor (prev index/term), the appended entry, the acknowledgement and the incumbent's committed index before the append. Each campaign-request event now carries the identity field 'leader' so the admission can be correlated in both streams.
experiment.responsibility: The raft module owns the higher-term authority rule that a node sheds leadership when it learns a newer term, and owns whether the log it accepts continues the committed prefix it already had.

comparisons.description: Control: the quorum-relevant follower does not grant the pre-vote while its leader context is intact.
Defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader must not be accepted through the inbound path.
Disruption: an up-to-date candidate must not take leadership at a higher term while the incumbent is still serving.
Bound: the deposed incumbent accepts the new leader's append and sheds leadership on the higher term rather than fighting it.
Bound: the new leader's anchor is exactly the incumbent's committed prefix (index 10, term 1), so no committed index is lost by the change.
Bound: after the append the deposed incumbent follows the new leader rather than remaining leaderless.

experiment.revision_reason: Same harness and same six comparisons, with one field added: both q_prevote_request emissions now carry the campaign identity field ('leader': 3) that the admission alias requires, so the campaign admission can be correlated in both streams and the three bound comparisons (incumbent becomes StateFollower, anchor equals the committed prefix, incumbent follows the new leader) can be evaluated instead of ending as 'Missing operation admission fields or identity'.
